描述_EN: the 20th century saw soft toys or dolls that served as marketing tools and souvenirs, as well as gifts for small children. two other examples in the museum’s theatre & performance collection are the felt totem girl in rose marie, 1925, and the cotton doll of lupino lane as bill snibson in me and my girl, 1937. with its trademark quiff of red hair and lopsided smile, it captures the essence of tweedy’s zany character and capacity for making audiences laugh. it represents the popular clown tweedy, created by the scottish performer alan digweed who appears annually with giffords circus and cirque berserk, in plays and pantomime, and in his one-man show. souvenir items associated with performance have long been produced for sale, most frequently in the 19th century when the best-selling items were ceramic figures based on performers. this soft toy continues the tradition. the toy was commissioned by tweedy, who sells it at venues where he appears and through his own website.
描述_ZN: 20世纪出现了作为营销工具和纪念品的软体玩具或娃娃，以及给小孩子的礼物。 博物馆的戏剧和表演藏品中的另外两个例子是1925年《Rose Marie》中的毡制图腾女孩，以及1937年《我和我的女孩》中Lupino Lane扮演Bill Snibson的棉花娃娃。 具有标志性的红色头发和倾斜的微笑，它抓住了Tweedy的古怪性格和使观众发笑的能力的本质。 它代表了流行的小丑Tweedy，由苏格兰表演者Alan Digweed创造，他每年都会出现在Giffords马戏团和Cirque Berserk，在戏剧和哑剧中，以及在他的单人表演中。 与表演有关的纪念品长期以来一直被生产销售，最常见的是在19世纪，当时最畅销的物品是以表演者为原型的陶瓷人物。 这个软玩具延续了这个传统。 这个玩具是由Tweedy委托的，他在他出现的地方和他自己的网站上销售。
